items: A run of fence along +X: posts every few metres and horizontal rails. add_fence sits each leg on the ground at its centre and leans it down the slope it crosses (the record's rz); a leg steeper than 15% is cut into 5 m pieces, each at its own height.
A clipped hedge — a green block len x h x w, 0.4-6 m tall. Placed like a fence: on the ground, leaning along its run.
The upstand between a pavement and the road.

A round-crowned tree: trunk plus a sphere canopy, h tall over all. A real one is 6-20 m with a 3-8 m crown — an absolute size that never scales with the block. It stands on the ground under its own trunk.
A cone on a short trunk — spruce, fir, pine. h tall, 2r across. A real one is 8-25 m.
A slim trunk with fronds arching out of the top. A real one is 5-15 m.
A low squashed dome of foliage, 0.4-2 m tall. Every shrub of a bed stands upright on the ground under it.

A planted rectangle raised a little above the ground. gx and gz are the ground slope (rise per metre) along the bed's own x and z: the slab is SHEARED onto that plane while the record stays upright. add_garden_bed fills them in, and tiles the bed when the ground under it is not planar.
A street light: tapered pole with a lantern at the top. A real one is 3-6 m.
A timber seat on two legs, seat top at h. It stands on the ground under it.
A cylindrical litter bin with a dark lid.
A strip of pavement running along +X. gx/gz shear it onto the ground plane, like the flower bed.

One marked bay: a thin slab with white lines on three sides. gx/gz are the ground slope along the bay's own x and z and shear the slab onto it. add_parking refuses ground more than 0.5 m off a plane or steeper than 8% — flatten_pad it first.

An arc of carriageway around the point you click, from angle a0 to a1 (0 = east, 90 = north). An arc cannot be sheared as a quad, so add_curved_road lays it on the ground plane with the record's own rx/rz tilt instead — it is a thin slab, so leaning it is right.
